candidates.attacker_control: The submitted password (rawPassword) is attacker-controlled request data in credential flows (UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.obtainPassword, BasicAuthenticationFilter.extractAndDecodeHeader, custom filters, or direct AuthenticationManager callers). The stored password (prefixEncodedPassword) is account data (e.g., a NULL password column, or a UserDetailsService/LDAP-mapped account provisioned without a password). Where both are null, no guessable secret is required: the mere absence of both values is treated as a match.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked in-framework callers for reachability: UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter converts a null password parameter to "" (web/.../authentication/UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.java:112-127), BasicAuthenticationFilter always yields a non-null (possibly empty) credential, and DaoAuthenticationProvider throws BadCredentialsException when authentication.getCredentials() == null (core/.../dao/DaoAuthenticationProvider.java:84-90); so the null/null branch is not reachable through those stock filters/providers and requires a custom filter or direct AuthenticationManager caller. Also verified the class Javadoc (lines 106-115) documents an IllegalArgumentException for an unmapped/null id, i.e., the early success return contradicts the documented fail-closed contract, and that no other guard in the method handles the both-null case, while the unmapped-id path itself still fails closed (UnmappedIdPasswordEncoder, lines 227-240).
candidates.impact: Authentication bypass / account impersonation for accounts whose stored password is null: the account can be logged into without knowing any secret, yielding that account's authorities and protected resources reachable through them. Because the affected class is the default delegating encoder in the affected lines, the flawed decision sits in a shared credential-verification primitive; scope is limited to accounts with null stored passwords plus an entry point that forwards a null credential.
candidates.prerequisites: (1) Application uses DelegatingPasswordEncoder directly or via PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder() (the default encoder in the affected 4.2.x/5.x configurations) together with a DaoAuthenticationProvider-style provider; (2) at least one account whose UserDetails.getPassword() is null (NULL password column, externally/SSO-provisioned account, or custom UserDetails implementation); (3) an authentication entry point that forwards a null credential instead of the empty string to PasswordEncoder.matches — the stock UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter converts a missing parameter to "" and DaoAuthenticationProvider rejects null credentials before calling the encoder, so a custom/other filter or a direct AuthenticationManager caller is required. Precondition (3) is the main uncertainty.
candidates.title: DelegatingPasswordEncoder.matches() returns true for a null raw password and a null stored password (credential check fails open)
candidates.trace: Credential entry (e.g., AuthenticationManager.authenticate(new UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(username, null))) -> AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.authenticate (core/.../dao/AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.java:126-198) -> DaoAuthenticationProvider.additionalAuthenticationChecks (core/.../dao/DaoAuthenticationProvider.java:75-102) -> adaptor PasswordEncoder.isPasswordValid -> delegate.matches(rawPass, encPass) (DaoAuthenticationProvider.java:157-177) -> DelegatingPasswordEncoder.matches(null, null) returns true at crypto/.../DelegatingPasswordEncoder.java:191-193 -> no BadCredentialsException -> createSuccessAuthentication (AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.java:217-229) -> authenticated token in the SecurityContext, so later authorization decisions (core/.../access/intercept/AbstractSecurityInterceptor.java:184-275; web/.../access/intercept/FilterSecurityInterceptor.java) treat the request as authenticated for that account.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; no test sources exist in the snapshot to confirm intended behavior. Upstream post-fix revision was not available offline, so it cannot be excluded that this early return is intentional upstream behavior at this revision rather than the patched defect; if intentional, this is a design weakness rather than the fixed vulnerability. The existence of null-password accounts and of a null-credential-forwarding entry point in a deployment are environment-dependent and not determinable from the source tree.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Authentication / authentication bypass from missing null handling in a credential comparison (CWE-287; CWE-476-adjacent)

coverage_summary: Per get_source_scope: 1,317 model-visible files, 0 over the 5 MiB limit, 0 excluded by sensitive-name/path filters, 0 excluded symlinks; binary-like files are refused/skipped. The snapshot contains no test sources (e.g., core/src/test is absent), so no test-driven confirmation was possible. Reviewed in depth: web filter chain and firewall (FilterChainProxy, StrictHttpFirewall/DefaultHttpFirewall, FirewalledResponse), CSRF (CsrfFilter, CookieCsrfTokenRepository, HttpSessionCsrfTokenRepository), remember-me (AbstractRememberMeServices, TokenBased/PersistentTokenBased services, JdbcTokenRepositoryImpl), authentication filters (UsernamePassword, Basic, Anonymous, RememberMe, SwitchUser, X509/SubjectDn extractor, pre-auth, CAS hooks), session/context persistence (HttpSessionSecurityContextRepository, SessionManagementFilter, ConcurrentSessionFilter, session-fixation strategies), access decision/interception (AbstractSecurityInterceptor, FilterSecurityInterceptor, Affirmative/Consensus/UnanimousBased, WebExpressionVoter/WebSecurityExpressionRoot), URL matchers (AntPath/Regex/MediaType/IpAddress), request cache/redirect helpers (DefaultSavedRequest, HttpSessionRequestCache, AbstractAuthenticationTargetUrlRequestHandler, DefaultRedirectStrategy), ACL/JDBC classes (BasicLookupStrategy, JdbcMutableAclService, JdbcTokenRepositoryImpl), LDAP authentication, and the core/crypto PasswordEncoder implementations plus PasswordEncoderFactories, PasswordEncoderUtils and DaoAuthenticationProvider. Sampled but not exhaustively read: config annotation/namespace classes, openid, cas/jackson2, data, samples, docs, sandbox. Repo-wide searches were run for XXE, deserialization, dynamic SQL, process execution and insecure randomness patterns. The snapshot appears to be the Spring Security 4.2.x line (gradle.properties 4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT; deprecated org.springframework.security.authentication.encoding package present; no WebFlux/oauth2/5.1-only classes).
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so expected-behavior/test-name corroboration and runtime validation were impossible.

No network/VCS access: the pre-fix/post-fix upstream state of the affected files could not be compared, so whether the reported behavior is the patched defect or intentional upstream behavior at this revision remains unverified.

Version metadata in the tree (4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT) coexists with crypto-module code carrying newer @since tags, so the exact upstream commit/branch point and therefore the exact security fix associated with this snapshot could not be pinned down from source alone.

Runtime reachability of the null/null credential path depends on application configuration (a caller forwarding a null credential and accounts with null stored passwords) that is not determinable from library source; the stock UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter/BasicAuthenticationFilter/DaoAuthenticationProvider paths do not reach it.
Large areas (config annotation DSL, openid, cas/jackson2, data, samples, docs) were only sampled, not exhaustively reviewed.

rejected_leads.lead: Deprecated core PlaintextPasswordEncoder.isPasswordValid (core/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/authentication/encoding/PlaintextPasswordEncoder.java:53-68) builds pass1 with 'encPass + ""', so a null stored password becomes the literal string "null"; a login submitting the password "null" is then matched by PasswordEncoderUtils.equals. It is the default encoder installed by new DaoAuthenticationProvider() (core/.../dao/DaoAuthenticationProvider.java:67-69) and is reachable through the normal form-login path.
rejected_leads.reason: Kept as a rejected (unconfirmed) lead rather than a second candidate: the precondition (an account whose stored password is null, no SaltSource configured) is narrow, and without the upstream fix revision it cannot be confirmed as the patched defect; its root cause is related to but distinct from the submitted candidate, and only one candidate may be submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: crypto/.../password/NoOpPasswordEncoder.java:38-40 matches an empty submitted password against an empty stored password (and a stored '{noop}' with empty plaintext), allowing login by omitting the password field.
rejected_leads.reason: Empty-password-equals-empty-stored-password is arguably expected behavior for a deprecated no-op encoder and is materially weaker evidence than the null/null success return; not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: PasswordEncoderUtils.equals (both copies) returns true for (null, null) because both lengths compute to -1 and the loop never executes.
rejected_leads.reason: Traced every caller (PlaintextPasswordEncoder, MessageDigestPasswordEncoder/Md4PasswordEncoder in both packages, LdapShaPasswordEncoder); each either passes non-null 'expected' values or dereferences first, so (null, null) is unreachable there; retained only as context.

rejected_leads.lead: Firewall/matcher/CSRF/remember-me/redirect/JDBC areas as hardening opportunities (StrictHttpFirewall, AntPathRequestMatcher/RegexRequestMatcher, CsrfFilter, TokenBasedRememberMeServices, AbstractAuthenticationTargetUrlRequestHandler, JdbcTokenRepositoryImpl).
rejected_leads.reason: On inspection these follow the shipped 4.2.x design and fail closed (firewall is the FilterChainProxy default and rejects non-printable ASCII and encoded slash/period/percent/backslash/semicolon; CSRF comparison fails closed; remember-me signature comparison is constant-time style; JDBC SQL is parameterized). No source-level bypass identified.

Only WebXmlMappableAttributesRetriever parses XML and it reads the container's own web.xml, not attacker input; SQL is parameterized; no process execution found; Math.random/new Random hits are JavaScript/sample assets. No evidence of a repository vulnerability in these areas.

rejected_leads.lead: LDAP empty-password handling as an anonymous-bind bypass.
rejected_leads.reason: The empty-password rejection is present (ldap/.../AbstractLdapAuthenticationProvider.java:77-83 and ldap/.../BindAuthenticator.java:77-81), so the classic LDAP empty-password bypass is already mitigated.

summary: Scope: the whole assigned tree reported by get_source_scope (1,317 readable files; binaries skipped by the NUL-byte policy; no sensitive-path or symlink exclusions). The snapshot is the Spring Security 4.2.x line (gradle.properties version 4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT; the deprecated org.springframework.security.authentication.encoding package is still present; no WebFlux/oauth2/5.1-only classes) with all test sources stripped, pointing at the ~Dec 2018\u2013Apr 2019 (4.2.13) development window. I traced attacker-controlled request data into the main trust boundaries: the FilterChainProxy firewall, CSRF filter/token repositories, remember-me token handling, session/context persistence, access-decision and interception logic, URL matchers, redirect/request-cache helpers, ACL/JDBC repositories, LDAP authentication, and both the core and crypto PasswordEncoder implementations. The single strongest source-evidenced candidate is the crypto DelegatingPasswordEncoder.matches() early success return when both the supplied and stored password are null; it is a credential check that fails open, contradicting the class's own documented fail-closed handling of an absent/unmapped id and affecting the encoder returned by PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder(). Related null/empty-password oddities (deprecated PlaintextPasswordEncoder turning a null stored password into the string \"null\"; NoOpPasswordEncoder matching \"\") are reported only as rejected leads because their attacker paths/preconditions are weaker. No runtime confirmation was performed and no upstream revision comparison was possible offline; confidence is therefore medium and requires the null-credential-forwarding precondition noted on the candidate.
